author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing reads a page before the first as the first page
summary: Asking for the owner listing at a page before the first shows an error page instead of the listing. The listing must read any such page as the first page and list the matches as normal.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner listing at a page before the first, when it runs, then the first page of matches is listed rather than an error page
the same holds for every page value below the first, not only the one immediately below it
given a request for the first page or for a later page that exists, when it runs, then the listing behaves as it does today
non_goals: a request for a page beyond the last page
a page value that is not a number
paging behavior of the veterinarian directory
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1, which records the owner's request verbatim: 'the owner listing treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200)'. No decisions beyond the request were recorded, so scope is held to pages below the first. Pages beyond the last, and non-numeric page values, are undecided and recorded under PRD Open Questions rather than resolved here. No Non-Goals row changed; no existing requirement contradicted. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already places this fix. architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row, states that normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding rather than a business rule, so the clamp belongs in OwnerController and nothing moves toward a domain core. system-design.md Contracts already names OwnerController as the owner of paged owner search; this dispatch added REQ-OWN-005 to that row and a clause naming the lower-bound normalization. No new package, type, pattern, or dependency. The cause is direct: processFindForm passes the raw page through to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, which computes page - 1 and hands it to PageRequest.of, and that factory rejects a negative index by throwing, which surfaces as the error page. Basis for the covering claim is a direct read of OwnerController.java lines 94-137 plus greps of the briefs; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker grep-and-read basis rather than a symbol resolution.
integration_points: Repository boundary: the new test crosses OwnerRepository through the class-level @MockitoBean already wired into OwnerControllerTests. A framework stub is the conscious exception testing-principles.md Mocking Policy allows: the fixture is class-scoped and shared by every test in the class, so a per-test hand-written double would fork a second repository seam inside one @WebMvcTest context. The new test reuses the existing fixture and adds no new stub.

Transport boundary: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock per testing-principles.md, drives the real dispatch, binding, and conversion machinery. It is what makes the assertion meaningful here, since the defect lives in what the handler does with a bound parameter.
Binding: no new entry point. GET /owners already binds Owner as a model attribute under setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"), and page stays a request-scoped int @RequestParam. Neither binding changes.
Repository contract unchanged: OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith keeps its signature. The normalization happens before the Pageable is built, so no persistence-side change is implied.

patterns.description: Web controller row of the pattern catalog: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range or shape is binding, which is what sanctions placing this fix in the controller
findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, the existing pagination helper that turns a one-based page into a zero-based PageRequest; the adjacent seam the fix follows
A rule the design doc assigns to the web controller is tested at the web level; extracting this clamp into a separate unit is placement drift, not pyramid progress

risks.risk: Clamping after the subtraction rather than before it. Math.max(page - 1, 0) reads as equivalent but overflows for Integer.MIN_VALUE, where page - 1 wraps to Integer.MAX_VALUE and yields a far page instead of the first. The second acceptance criterion covers every value below the first, not just zero.
risks.mitigation: Normalize the one-based page before any arithmetic, then derive the zero-based index from the normalized value (security-principles.md Trust Boundaries: validate type, range, and shape at the boundary before use).

risks.risk: Normalizing only inside the pagination helper. The repository call would then be correct while addPaginationModel still receives the raw value, so currentPage in the model, the page links, and the current-page highlight would render against a page that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the entry point in processFindForm so the repository call and the view model read the same value (architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller: bind, delegate, select the response).

risks.risk: Scope creep into the two open paging questions. A page beyond the last and a non-numeric page value are PRD Open Questions and prd-entry non-goals; the vet directory pages independently and is also a non-goal.
risks.mitigation: Change only the lower bound on the owner listing. Leave the upper bound and the type-conversion failure exactly as they behave today, and leave VetController untouched.

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to judge. Design-doc write this dispatch: docs/system-design.md Contracts, the OwnerController row. REQ-OWN-005 joins its Implements list, satisfying contracts-sync, and the Purpose cell gains a clause naming the lower-bound normalization as a guarantee of the type. No ADR: the placement follows a rule the architecture brief already states, and no alternative is foreclosed for a future slice. Known Defects in system-design.md is not extended, because that table records confirmed defects that remain in the code and this one is fixed in the same slice. Test-name caution for the implementer: the prd-entry proposes processFindFormTreatsPageBelowFirstAsFirstPage, which names the handler method, while testing-principles.md Test Naming sets the BDD school the{Subject}Should{Outcome} as the bar a reviewer applies and rejects that shape by example. Prefer a behavior name such as theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowTheFirstAsTheFirstPage; the prd-entry field is a suggestion and the testing brief is the reviewer's bar. Existing tests all request page=1 explicitly and the parameterless default is already 1, so the third acceptance criterion is well covered by the current suite.
